correctness.rationale: Exact sampled 3x3 proximal maps produce a positive 6x6 covariance operator with determinant \(\det(I-C)=-tF(t)/(16(2t+1)^3)\). The positive Lyapunov matrix at \(t=1/2\) proves one stable side; \(\det(I-C(2))=-13/125\) and cone Perron continuity identify the unique positive root of F as the exact transition. Positive 2-step covariance and observability determinants transfer nondecay and exponential growth to the primal squared iterate for a compatible initialization; the included checker verifies all determinant identities, direct state steps and polynomial witnesses. Finite tests are algebra checks, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The two convex clients are a natural minimal maximally heterogeneous sample while their average is strongly convex. The sharp quintic boundary classifies an entire stepsize axis and exposes exponentially growing expected squared primal error despite signed-mean convergence, giving a meaningful analytical benchmark for moment stability of variance-reduced proximal stochastic methods. Narrow scope and no extrapolation to general problems are expressly recorded.
